newsitem.title: USA: Huntco sees continued pressure on margins.
newsitem.headline: Huntco sees continued pressure on margins.

text.p: Huntco Inc said it anticipates its fiscal 1997 fourth quarter sales to exceed its record second quarter level of $84 million but expects gross profit margins to remain under pressure.

While gross profit margins have begun to slowly recover, they are expected to remain under pressure during the quarter as the company continues to shift its supplier base to lower its raw material costs, Huntco said. This process should be largely accomplished during the fourth quarter, it added.
Earlier, Huntco said fiscal 1997 third quarter sales rose 7.2 percent over the same period last year to $73.4 million.
Earnings for its third quarter ended January 31, 1997 fell to $100,000 or $0.02 a share from $2.2 million or $0.24 for the prior year's third quarter.

Higher fiscal third quarter sales reflect increased levels of tons processed. Huntco said it processed 210,864 tons of steel in the quarter ended January 31, 1997, an increase of 5.6 percent over the same period a year earlier.

The company said that gross margins came under pressure late in its second quarter of fiscal 1997 and that this margin pressure extended into the third quarter. This narrowing of gross profit margins was primarily due to higher domestic prices for its primary raw material, hot rolled steel coils, as significant quantities of lower priced imported material were available in its market territories.

Huntco also said it began operations at a new facility in South Carolina during January, 1997 and is currently doubling capacity at its cold rolling operations in Blytheville, Ark. It also will install and start-up a new coil slitting line at its South Carolina facility during March, 1997.
Due to these factors and current market conditions, gross profit margins in the fourth quarter are only expected to increase to around nine percent, it said.
